## Data Model
User config only: `providers: {<name>: {via: claude|codex|gemini|aws, model?: string, region?: string}}`.

## Implementation Approach
`arena-run.sh` is a small FETCHER: parse args, refuse in a worker, load the provider from the config
(`jq -e`), dispatch on `via` to one function per runner that builds an argv array (no `eval`, the prompt
passed as one argument or, for aws, as a JSON messages document built with `jq -n --rawfile`), run it
under `timeout`, print stdout; `--check` loops the providers. The launcher change is one token pair.
The two commands gain prose steps that call the runner with the Bash tool.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: arena-run.sh core
```bash
[ "${HEFESTO_WORKER:-}" = 1 ] && die "arena-run: runs from the pane, never from a launched worker (a second vendor from inside a sandboxed worker is egress the sandbox exists to stop)"
P=$(jq -ce --arg n "$NAME" '.providers[$n]' "$CONFIG") || die "arena-run: no provider '$NAME' in $CONFIG (.providers)"
VIA=$(jq -r .via <<<"$P"); MODEL=$(jq -r '.model // empty' <<<"$P")
case "$VIA" in
  claude) CMD=(claude -p "$(cat "$F")" --permission-mode plan); [ -n "$MODEL" ] && CMD+=(--model "$MODEL") ;;
  codex)  CMD=(codex exec --sandbox read-only); [ -n "$MODEL" ] && CMD+=(-m "$MODEL"); CMD+=("$(cat "$F")") ;;
  gemini) CMD=(gemini -p "$(cat "$F")"); [ -n "$MODEL" ] && CMD+=(-m "$MODEL") ;;
  aws)    [ "$PURPOSE" = arena ] && die "arena-run: $NAME (aws) is a message API — it cannot read the repository; use it for --second-opinion"
          [ -n "$MODEL" ] || die "arena-run: $NAME via aws needs a model"
          MSG=$(jq -nc --rawfile t "$F" '[{role:"user",content:[{text:$t}]}]')
          CMD=(aws bedrock-runtime converse --model-id "$MODEL" --messages "$MSG"); R=$(jq -r '.region // empty' <<<"$P"); [ -n "$R" ] && CMD+=(--region "$R") ;;
  *) die "arena-run: provider $NAME has via '$VIA' (expected claude, codex, gemini or aws)" ;;
esac
command -v "${CMD[0]}" >/dev/null || die "arena-run: ${CMD[0]} not found — $(hint "$VIA")"
out=$(timeout "$TO" "${CMD[@]}" 2>"$err"); rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] || die "arena-run: $NAME exited $rc: $(tail -1 "$err")"
[ "$VIA" = aws ] && out=$(jq -r '.output.message.content[0].text' <<<"$out")
printf '%s\n' "$out"
```

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Foreign CLIs change their flags | the runner breaks | one function per runner, `--check` names the CLI, the user's real run (SC-004) is the evidence |
| A foreign reader writes to the repo | edits from an unreviewed vendor | codex `--sandbox read-only`, claude `--permission-mode plan`; gemini has no read-only flag in its documented headless mode — documented; the plan-phase write-block does not cover a separate process; the arena runs from the pane where the user sees the process; the merge reads `arena/<p>.md` only |
| Repository content leaves the machine to a second vendor | data egress | opt-in per provider; the runner refuses in a worker; docs state it plainly |
| A foreign second opinion treated as approval | a gate passed by a weaker or unranked reviewer | it never writes `## Reviewed`; the label says "not the gate" |

## Plan review 2026-10-02 (fresh `code-reviewer`, REVISE_PLAN, 7 changes; sandbox and argv limits measured) — applied
1. **Host check**, the launcher's FR-020 twin: `--check` and the run path refuse when `$HOME` is not
   writable (a sandboxed shell — measured: `~/.claude` and `~/.codex` unwritable here, egress filtered);
   both commands and `docs/install.md` say `--via` and `--second-opinion` run from an unsandboxed pane.
2. **Prompt on stdin**, never argv (MAX_ARG_STRLEN 128 KiB; a 2,000-line diff of this repo measured
   190 KB): claude/codex/gemini read stdin, aws takes `--messages file://`; the code-mode diff is also
   capped at 96 KiB; stubs record stdin length; one case feeds a >128 KiB prompt.
3. **aws flags** verified on aws-cli 2.32: `--output json --cli-read-timeout 0 --no-cli-pager
   --inference-config maxTokens=<n>`.
4. **codex** relays only `--output-last-message`, never its progress stdout (whose `path:line` tokens
   the cite check would read as claims).
5. **Launcher test at the tool-call level**: the existing fake `claude` records `HEFESTO_WORKER` from
   its environment; the dry-run assertion at the launcher's `^claude -p` check becomes `^env
   HEFESTO_WORKER=1 claude -p`; mutation "drop the env pair" → red.
6. **Provider names** `[a-z0-9_]+` (they become `tiers=` tokens `arena-metrics` reads).
7. Nits: `timeout -k 10`, default 540 (below the tool's 600 s), die on empty output, gemini never
   `--yolo`, foreign slots and the second opinion run with `run_in_background` alongside the scouts and
   the gate, the relayed second opinion wrapped as data, this repo's own config would use tier aliases
   for a `claude` provider.
